title: In vivo proximity-labeling with miniTurboID to screen for protein-protein interactions in the filamentous ascomycete Sordaria macrospora
author: Hollstein, Groth, et al.
materials: Dried peptide samples were reconstituted in 20 µl LC-MS sample buffer (2 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid). 2 to 8 µl of each sample were subjected to reverse phase liquid chromatography for peptide separation using an RSLCnano Ultimate 3000 system (Thermo Fisher Scientific): Peptides were loaded on an Acclaim PepMap 100 pre-column (100 µm x 2 cm, C18, 5 µm, 100 Å; Thermo Fisher Scientific) with 0.07 % trifluoroacetic acid at a flow rate of 20 µL/min for 3 min. Analytical separation of peptides was done on an Acclaim PepMap RSLC column (75 µm x 50 cm, C18, 2 µm, 100 Å; Thermo Fisher Scientific) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min. The solvent composition was gradually changed within 94 min from 96 % solvent A (0.1 % formic acid) and 4 % solvent B (80 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid) to 10 % solvent B within 2 min, to 30 % solvent B within the next 58 min, to 45 % solvent B within the following 22 min, and to 90 % solvent B within the last 12 min of the gradient. All solvents and acids had Optima grade for LC-MS (Fisher Chemical). Eluting peptides were on-line ionized by nano-electrospray (nESI) using the Nanospray Flex Ion Source (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 1.5 kV (liquid junction) and transferred into a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Full scans in a mass range of 300 to 1650 m/z were recorded at a resolution of 30,000 followed by data-dependent top 10 HCD fragmentation at a resolution of 15,000 (dynamic exclusion enabled). LC-MS method programming and data acquisition was performed with the XCalibur 4.0 software (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

The identification of the already known SmSTRIPAK components using the SCI1 subunit with either ligase demonstrates that both, TurboID and miniTurboID, can be used to reliably screen for protein-protein interactions. Due to the reduced size of miniTurboID (32 kDa), we speculate that it is less likely to interfere with the native function or localization of the POI as compared to the larger TurboID ligase (39 kDa). Furthermore, our miniTurboID construct demonstrates that the small ligase is functional when including the TurboID-specific mutations M241T and S263P. Consequently, miniTurboID can be easily cloned from existing TurboID vectors in a single PCR amplification reaction. For establishing the BioID proximity labeling methodology in other filamentous fungi, we suggest to test both ligases for their functionality and their compatibility with the POI e.g. by complementation of the knockout with the POI-ligase fusion protein.

steps.title: Prepare safety and materials
steps.instruction: Wear fresh vinyl or powder‑free nitrile gloves; avoid any plastic containers for solvents and do not use glassware that has been cleaned in a dishwasher.

steps.title: Extract proteins from frozen mycelium
steps.instruction: Grind frozen mycelium in liquid nitrogen, transfer the powder to a Falcon tube, add 500 µL lysis buffer per gram of powder, vortex, heat 5 min at 65 °C, centrifuge 10 000 × g for 20 min at room temperature, and transfer the supernatant to a fresh microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Equilibrate Strep‑Tactin Sepharose resin
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL Strep‑Tactin Sepharose slurry (equivalent to 50 µL bed volume) into a tube, centrifuge 2 min at 400 × g, discard the storage buffer and wash the resin twice with 375 µL 1× Buffer W.

steps.title: Capture biotinylated proteins
steps.instruction: Remove Buffer W, add 1 mL crude protein extract (≈30 mg protein) to the resin, incubate 30 min on a rotating wheel, centrifuge 400 × g for 2 min, discard the unbound fraction.

steps.title: Wash resin with SDS buffer
steps.instruction: Wash the resin three times with 800 µL 1× Buffer W containing 0.4 % SDS; invert the tube five times to mix after each wash.

steps.title: Elute biotinylated proteins
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL 1× BXT to the resin, incubate 10 min on a rotating wheel ensuring contact, centrifuge and collect the eluate in a Protein LoBind tube; repeat once to obtain a total of 200 µL eluate.

steps.title: Split eluate for precipitation
steps.instruction: Divide the 200 µL eluate equally into two Protein LoBind tubes (100 µL each) for subsequent chloroform‑methanol precipitation.

steps.title: Perform chloroform‑methanol precipitation
steps.instruction: On ice, add 400 µL methanol to each 100 µL eluate, vortex 5 s; add 100 µL chloroform, vortex 5 s; add 300 µL water, vortex 15 s, then centrifuge 4 000 × g for 3 min. Discard the upper aqueous phase leaving 10–20 µL, add 300 µL methanol, vortex, centrifuge 20 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, remove supernatant, dry the pellet in a SpeedVac at 60 °C, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Reconstitute dried peptides for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Resuspend each dried peptide sample in 20 µL LC‑MS sample buffer (2 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid); inject 2–8 µL for analysis.

steps.title: Run LC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Load peptides onto an Acclaim PepMap 100 pre‑column (100 µm × 2 cm, C18, 5 µm, 100 Å) with 0.07 % TFA at 20 µL min⁻¹ for 3 min, then separate on an Acclaim PepMap RSLC analytical column (75 µm × 50 cm, C18, 2 µm, 100 Å) at 300 nL min⁻¹ using a 94‑min gradient (96 % A/4 % B to 10 % B in 2 min, to 30 % B in 58 min, to 45 % B in 22 min, to 90 % B in 12 min). Use Optima‑grade solvents, nano‑ESI at 1.5 kV, and acquire full scans 300–1650 m/z at 30 000 resolution followed by top‑10 HCD at 15 000 resolution with dynamic exclusion. Control acquisition with XCalibur 4.0.

steps.title: Configure MaxQuant for data processing
steps.instruction: Open MaxQuant v1.6.10.43, keep standard parameters, add variable modification “Biotinylation of Lysine” (Unimod #3), optionally add variable modification “Phospho (STY)”, activate label‑free quantification (LFQ), and set maximum missed cleavages to 3.

steps.title: Process data with Perseus
steps.instruction: Import proteinGroups.txt, use LFQ intensities, MS/MS counts, biotin site positions and Phospho(STY) positions; filter out rows marked ‘+’ in ‘only identified by site’, ‘reverse’ or ‘potential contaminant’; log2‑transform LFQ intensities; create two annotation groups (group 1: free TurboID vs SCI1‑TurboID; group 2: free TurboID vs SCI1‑miniTurboID); generate multi‑scatter plots; filter each group for at least three valid values; replace missing values with a normal distribution separately per column; generate volcano plots for each group (FDR = 0.01, s0 = 2); export significantly enriched proteins; replace imputed values by NaN.
